extractionNotes: Full extraction complete: all 4 Strands (Exploring Materials, Processes For Living, Vigour Behind Life, Relationships With The Environment) across all 3 Years (SHS 1-3) are captured in this file. Actual totals extracted: 30 Content Standards, 31 Learning Outcomes, 60 Learning Indicators (see the Scope-and-Sequence cross-check note below for why this is 60, not the table's claimed 61).

Document self-identifies internally as 'Core Science' in its own Rationale section (PDF page 22, printed page 20/21 area: 'The quality of Core Science instruction will create the foundation for the study of science...'), even though the cover title and every page footer read 'GENERAL SCIENCE'. Stored subject name is 'General Science' per the cover/footer/dominant usage; this internal alias is recorded here per the task brief rather than silently discarded.

SCOPE AND SEQUENCE summary table (PDF page 24, printed page 22) gives per-Sub-Strand-per-Year totals: Strand 1/Science and Materials in Nature: Y1 CS2 LO2 LI6, Y2 CS1 LO1 LI3, Y3 CS2 LO2 LI4. Strand 2/Essentials for Survival: Y1 CS2 LO3 LI5, Y2 CS2 LO2 LI6, Y3 CS2 LO2 LI6. Strand 3/Powering the future with energy forms: Y1 CS1 LO1 LI2, Y2 CS1 LO1 LI2, Y3 CS1 LO1 LI2. Strand 3/Forces acting on substances and mechanisms: Y1 CS1 LO1 LI2, Y2 CS1 LO1 LI1, Y3 CS1 LO1 LI2. Strand 3/Consumer Electronics: Y1 CS1 LO1 LI1, Y2 CS1 LO1 LI2, Y3 CS1 LO1 LI2. Strand 4/The Human Body and Health: Y1 CS3 LO3 LI3, Y2 CS1 LO1 LI2, Y3 CS2 LO2 LI4. Strand 4/Technology in our Local Industries: Y1 CS2 LO2 LI3, Y2 CS1 LO1 LI2, Y3 CS1 LO1 LI1. Grand totals per the table: 30 CS / 31 LO / 61 LI. NOTE: in the raw -layout text extraction, the table's 'S/N 4 Relationships With The Environment' row label visually sits beside the 'Consumer Electronics' row rather than 'The Human Body and Health' row (a multi-line-cell wrapping artifact of the source table, not a pdftotext bug we introduced) - the in-body Strand/Sub-Strand curriculum codes (Consumer Electronics is coded 1.3.3/2.3.3/3.3.3, i.e. Strand 3; The Human Body and Health is coded 1.4.1/2.4.1/3.4.1, i.e. Strand 4) confirm the grouping actually used throughout the body content and in this file: Strand 3 'Vigour Behind Life' has three sub-strands (Powering the Future with Energy Forms, Forces Acting on Substances and Mechanisms, Consumer Electronics); Strand 4 'Relationships With The Environment' has two sub-strands (The Human Body and Health, Technology in our Local Industries).

Cross-check performed: summing every actually-extracted Learning Indicator in the body against the Scope and Sequence table's per-cell figures matches exactly for every Sub-Strand/Year EXCEPT Year 1, Strand 3, Sub-Strand 'Forces Acting on Substances and Mechanisms' (code 1.3.2), where the table predicts Content Standard 1.3.2.CS.1 should have 2 Learning Indicators (LI=2 in the table cell) but the body only prints ONE Learning Indicator (1.3.2.LI.1) under 1.3.2.CS.1, with only one Assessment block (1.3.2.AS.1) following it before the sub-strand's Teaching and Learning Resources section begins. No second Learning Indicator or Assessment code for 1.3.2 appears anywhere in the document. This is preserved verbatim (not invented) and flagged NEEDS_REVIEW on that Content Standard. This single discrepancy exactly accounts for the difference between the table's claimed grand total of 61 Learning Indicators and the 60 actually printed/extracted in the body.

Content Standard codes are confirmed NOT globally unique in this document (matching the cross-subject quirk already documented in docs/curriculum-extraction-schema.md item 2): Assessment/Learning-Indicator numbering restarts at .1 for every new Content Standard, e.g. both 1.1.1.CS.1 and 1.1.1.CS.2 (different Content Standards under the same Sub-Strand) each have their own LI.1/LI.2/LI.3 and AS.1/AS.2/AS.3. The natural key for a Learning Indicator in this file is therefore (Year/Strand, SubStrand, ContentStandard, Sequence), not the printed code string alone.

Two Content Standard codes are printed without their separating dots: '1.4.1CS2' (Year 1, Strand 4, Sub-Strand 'The Human Body and Health', should read '1.4.1.CS.2' by the document's own pattern) and '3.1.1CS2' (Year 3, Strand 1, Sub-Strand 'Science and Materials in Nature', should read '3.1.1.CS.2'). Both preserved verbatim as printed and flagged NEEDS_REVIEW on the affected Content Standard.

Several Assessment codes are printed garbled with a stray 'x.' segment: '1.x.3.1.AS.2' (Year 1, Strand 3 Sub-Strand 'Powering the Future with Energy Forms', Content Standard 1.3.1.CS.1, attached to Learning Indicator 1.3.1.LI.2; expected '1.3.1.AS.2'), '3.x.2.1.AS.3' (Year 3, Strand 2, Content Standard 3.2.1.CS.1, attached to Learning Indicator 3.2.1.LI.3; expected '3.2.1.AS.3'), and '3.x.2.1.AS.2' (Year 3, Strand 2, Content Standard 3.2.1.CS.2, attached to Learning Indicator 3.2.1.LI.2; expected '3.2.1.AS.2'). All preserved verbatim and flagged NEEDS_REVIEW on the affected Learning Indicator/Assessment.

Structural difference from the Biomedical Science extraction of this same pipeline: in this document, 'Teaching and Learning Resources' (TLR) is printed once per Content Standard (inside/immediately after that Content Standard's own Learning-Indicators-and-Assessment table), not once per Sub-Strand. This file therefore attaches teachingLearningResources/teachingLearningResourcesHeaderSeen/source_TLR at the contentStandards[] level rather than the subStrands[] level, per the task instruction to attach Category B fields 'at whichever level it's actually printed'.

National Core Values / National Values labelling is inconsistent verbatim across the document ('National Core Values:', 'National Values', 'National Values:' all occur) and is recorded per Learning Outcome in guidance.nationalCoreValuesHeaderSeen exactly as printed, per the task instruction not to normalise this wording.

Minor verbatim typos preserved without correction: 'embrac diversity' (should be 'embrace', Year 1 1.1.1.LO.2 GESI text), 'Subject GENERALSCIENCE' (missing space, heading for Year 3 Strand 4 Sub-Strand 'Technology in Local Industries', page 113).

Strand/Sub-Strand name spelling varies by Year in the source and is stored as printed for each Year occurrence (per the cross-subject schema note that a Strand's own name can differ between Years): Strand 4 prints as 'RELATIONSHIPS WITH THE ENVIRONMENT' (plural) at its Year 1 and Year 3 headings but 'RELATIONSHIP WITH THE ENVIRONMENT' (singular) at its Year 2 heading. Sub-Strand 'Technology in our Local Industries' prints with 'our' at the Year 1 heading but as 'Technology in Local Industries' (no 'our') at the Year 2 and Year 3 headings. Sub-Strand 'Consumer Electronics' prints in all caps at Year 1 and Year 3 headings but in title case ('3. Consumer Electronics') at the Year 2 heading.

Front matter (PDF pages 1-24, printed pages i-22): shared SHS boilerplate (SHS Curriculum Overview, Philosophy/Vision/Goal/Rationale of General/Core Science, 21st-Century Skills, GESI, SEL's Five Core Competencies, Learning and Teaching Approaches, UDL, the Bloom's/Webb's DoK framework, Curriculum Development Panel list, and the Scope-and-Sequence summary table) is document-level context per the schema's Phase 5 design notes and is not re-extracted per-node.

Page provenance method: 'page' values are the printed footer page number (format 'GENERAL SCIENCE | N' or 'N | GENERAL SCIENCE' in the -layout pdftotext extraction), reliably related to the raw PDF page index by 'page = pdfPageIndex - 2' throughout the entire body (verified by independent single-page pdftotext pulls at multiple points including the document's final pages). Sub-Strand heading and Content Standard table start pages were individually verified against footer markers; Learning Outcome pages within a Sub-Strand that has more than one Learning Outcome are approximated to the nearest preceding footer marker where a table spans a page break, since the 2-column -layout text stream does not always preserve strict top-to-bottom reading order across a page boundary. Learning Indicators and Assessment blocks inherit their parent Content Standard's page; Teaching and Learning Resources source page is recorded separately (source_TLR) where it is visibly on a later page than its Content Standard's own table start.

learningOutcomes.description: Evaluate the characteristics of science.

guidance.twentyFirstCenturySkills: Communication and Collaboration: Learners work in teams and groups to discuss and share ideas about the characteristics of science. Critical Thinking: Acknowledging the different opinions of different characteristics of science: Consider personal reactions to situations or problems and how these reactions may influence thinking. Make simple modifications to known ideas and routine solutions to generate some different ideas and possibilities. Examine words that show reasons and words that show conclusions. Compare and contrast information and ideas in own and others' reasoning. Consider how reasons and examples are used to support a point of view and illustrate meaning. Consider ways to express and describe thinking activity, including the expression of feelings about learning, both to others and to self. Explore some learning strategies, including planning, repetition, rewording, memorisation and use of mnemonics. Investigate ways to problem-solve using experiential language. Use and give examples of different kinds of questions. Generate ideas that are new and make choices after considering personal preferences. Identify words that indicate components of a point of view. Use reasons and examples for different purposes. Express and describe the thinking activity. Practice some learning strategies. Demonstrate and articulate some problem-solving approaches. Digital Literacy: Learning from internet resources. Cultural identity: Explore instances of the application of characteristics of science that are similar to the national shared values - Respect, humility, loyalty, patriotism, etc.
guidance.gesi: When teaching the characteristics of science, it is important to consider GESI values to ensure an inclusive and equitable learning environment for all students: Promote the idea that all genders and abilities have equal abilities and potential in scientific fields. Ensure representation by highlighting the contributions of scientists from different genders throughout history and in contemporary science. Discuss how societal expectations and biases can influence perceptions of GESI roles in scientific fields and the importance of breaking free from these stereotypes. Promote collaborative learning environments where students work together in diverse teams, respecting each other's contributions and learning from one another. Encourage the value of diverse perspectives and experiences in scientific inquiry.
guidance.sel: Learners having experienced a science pedagogy that ensures social and emotional learning skills (SELS) and working with each other will lead to: working to build learners' self-confidence. regularly acknowledge students' strengths fostering an environment that supports relationship building among learners and between students and staff. allowing learners to have a decision-making role related to classroom activities and rules. help students accurately assess their own capabilities and qualities.

learningIndicators.description: Classify different solids and their uses.
pedagogicalExemplars: Talk for Learning: Through a whole class session, guide learners to use charts of the periodic table to review the grouping of elements into metals, semi-metals and non-metals.

Activity-based Learning: Using samples of metals, semi-metals and non-metallic materials, guide learners to identify and distinguish between their properties such as lustre, electrical and heat conductivity, density, malleability, ductility, tensile strength and sonority. Guide learners to work in pairs to distinguish between: 1. metals and non-metals 2. semi-metals and non-metals 3. metals and semi-metals. Assist learners in undertaking a practical activity to demonstrate the corrosion of metals and explain how corrosion or rusting can be prevented.

Individualised Learning: Work individually to create mind-maps that show the relationship between the characteristic properties of metals, semi-metals and non-metals and their respective uses and applications in daily life.
